model.name: commodity_reports_v1
model.description: Official crop/energy/metal reports tagged (commodity × country) so the dashboard's stage-2 country window can show what was published about that country's commodity. The report's text picks the country, not the publisher: a USDA release on Brazilian wheat belongs on BRA·wheat.
model.buckets: index[commodity][ISO3 | _global] -> item ids, most important first

learning.how: build_reports.py label --series-id ... --label promote; next build re-weights that series.

title.original: United States on track for record crude oil production in 2026

items.summary: We forecast U.S. crude oil production will average 13.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in 2026, surpassing the previous record of 13.7 million b/d set in 2025, in our latest Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO).

title.original: EIA expects record electricity generation in 2026 and 2027

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) expects U.S. electricity generation will grow 2.2% to a record 4,368 billion kilowatthours (BkWh) this year. EIA expects an additional 1.7% growth in electricity generation next year.

title.original: EIA expects a drop in global oil demand will limit price increases from Hormuz disruptions

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its June Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), reducing its expectation for global oil demand in 2026. High fuel prices, reduced fuel availability, and government initiatives are curbing oil consumption this year, particularly in Asia, resulting in the world consuming 1 million fewer barrels of oil each day on average than it did last year. The reduced demand could limit crude oil price increases resulting from near-term disruptions in the flow of oil out of the Middle East through the Strait of Hormuz.

title.original: Short-Term Energy Outlook

items.summary: (Wed, 09 Sep 2026) Global oil market assumptions. We forecast oil production in the Middle East will rise in the coming months because of gradually increasing flows through the Strait of Hormuz and the use of alternative routes out of the region, according to our September 2026 Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO). However, we assume some constraints to exporting oil from the Middle East will persist through the end of the year, which keeps crude oil production in the region below pre-conflict averages until the second quarter of 2027 (2Q27).

title.original: USDA Forecasts U.S. Corn Production Up and Soybean Production Down from 2024

items.summary: – The Crop Production report issued today by USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) forecasted corn production up from 2024 and soybean production down from last year. Corn production is up 13% from last year, forecast at 16.7 billion bushels; soybean growers are expected to decrease their production 2% from 2024, forecast at 4.29 billion bushels.

title.original: US corn production up while soybean production down from September

items.summary: According to the Crop Production report issued today by USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS), corn production is forecast at 15.2 billion bushels, up less than 1% from the previous forecast, but down 1% from last year; soybean growers are expected to increase their production 10% from 2023, forecast at 4.58 billion bushels.

title.original: USDA forecasts US corn production down and soybean production up from 2023

items.summary: The Crop Production report issued today by USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) forecasted corn production down from 2023 and soybean production up from last year. Corn production is down 1% from last year, forecast at 15.1 billion bushels; soybean growers are expected to increase their production 10% from 2023, forecast at a record high 4.59 billion bushels.

title.original: NASS to collect updated information on planted acreage

items.summary: In July, the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will collect updated information on 2022 acres planted to barley, canola, corn, dry edible beans, oats, sorghum, soybeans, sunflowers, and Durum and other spring wheat in three states. NASS previously collected planted acreage information during the first two weeks of June, with the results published in the June 30 Acreage report.

title.original: NASS suspends pecan estimates for December and January

items.summary: The Crop Production report to be published on Dec. 9, 2021, by the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will not contain forecasted pecan production estimates. Also, NASS will not publish the Pecan Production report in January 2022 that typically contains preliminary acreage, yield, production, price, and value estimates.

title.original: USDA NASS to Collect Additional Harvested Acreage Information

items.summary: Corn and soybeans in Iowa have been particularly impacted by the recent derecho. USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service will collect harvested acreage information for both crops in Iowa in preparation for the September 11 Crop Production report. These additional data will help to better assess the full impact. If the newly collected data justifies any changes, NASS will publish updated harvested acreage estimates in the September report.

title.original: USDA NASS to Re-Survey North Dakota Operators with Previously Unharvested Corn and Soybeans

items.summary: In May, USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will contact survey respondents in North Dakota who previously reported unharvested corn and/or soybean acreage. If the newly collected data justifies any changes, NASS will update the Jan. 10 estimates in the June 11 Crop Production report. Stocks estimates are also subject to review since unharvested production is included in the estimate of on-farm stocks.

title.original: USDA NASS to Re-Survey Operators with Previously Unharvested Corn and Soybeans

items.summary: Later this month, USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service will contact survey respondents in Michigan, Minnesota, South Dakota, and Wisconsin who previously reported unharvested corn and/or soybean acreage. If the newly collected data justifies any changes, NASS will update the Jan. 10 estimates in the May 12 Crop Production report. Stocks estimates are also subject to review since unharvested production is included in the estimate of on-farm stocks.

title.original: EIA increases global oil production forecast after the opening of the Strait of Hormuz

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its July Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO), increasing its expectations for global oil production.

title.original: EIA expects highest natural gas inventories in a decade heading into winter

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration expects natural gas inventories will increase to 3,985 billion cubic feet (Bcf) in October, the most gas in inventories ahead of the winter heating season since 2016.

title.original: USDA forecasts winter wheat production up 2% in 2025, orange production up slightly from April forecast

items.summary: – U.S. farmers are expected to produce 1.38 billion bushels of winter wheat this year, according to the Crop Production report released today by USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS).

title.original: USDA NASS to host webinar to highlight available data for recently discontinued programs

items.summary: U.S. farmers are expected to produce 1.28 billion bushels of winter wheat this year, according to the Crop Production report released today by USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS). In NASS’s first winter wheat production forecast for 2024, production is expected to increase 2% from 2023. As of May 1, the U.S. yield is expected to average 50.7 bushels per acre, up 0.1 bushel from last year’s average of 50.6 bushels per acre.

title.original: US corn ending stocks up 29% from last year, soybean ending stocks up 29%

items.summary: Old crop corn stocks on hand as of Sept. 1, 2024 totaled 1.76 billion bushels, up 29% from Sept. 1, 2023, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) Grain Stocks report released today. Old crop soybeans stored in all positions were up 29% from Sept. 1, 2023, and all wheat stocks were up 12% from a year earlier.

title.original: NASS to review acreage data

items.summary: In preparation for the August Crop Production report, USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will review all available data, including survey data and the latest information from USDA’s Farm Service Agency and Risk Management Agency, for planted and harvested acreage for barley, corn, cotton, dry edible beans, oats, peanuts, rice, sorghum, soybeans, sugarbeets, Durum wheat, other spring wheat, and winter wheat. If the data review justifies any changes, NASS will publish updated planted and harvested acreage estimates in the Aug. 12, 2024, report.

title.original: NASS to review small grain acreage information

items.summary: In preparation for the August Crop Production report, USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will review all available data, including survey data and the latest information from USDA’s Farm Service Agency and Risk Management Agency, for planted and harvested acreage for barley, oats, Durum wheat, other spring wheat, and winter wheat. If the data review justifies any changes, NASS will publish updated planted and harvested acreage estimates in the Aug. 11, 2023, report.

title.original: NASS Acreage report released on-time; Quickstats data delayed

items.summary: At Noon ET, USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) successfully released the Acreage report. The JSON, .txt, .pdf and .csv formats of the report are available at Today’s Reports on the NASS website and at Cornell’s Mann Library. Due to a technical issue, the 2023 Acreage data for Quickstats is delayed. The Grain Stocks and Rice Stocks Quickstats data are not impacted by this delay.

title.original: NASS to review acreage earlier for certain crops

items.summary: USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will review all available data, including survey data, satellite-based data, and the latest information from USDA’s Farm Service Agency and Risk Management Agency, for planted and harvested acreage for corn, cotton, peanuts, rice, sorghum, soybeans, and sugarbeets in preparation for the September Crop Production report. If the data review justifies any changes, NASS will publish updated planted and harvested acreage estimates in the Sept. 10 report.

title.original: EIA updates forecast amid continued Mideast disruption; will publish new energy security datasets

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration published its May Short-Term Energy Outlook, reflecting a continued disruption to Middle Eastern oil flows.

title.original: Wholesale Electricity Market Data

items.summary: (Thu, 03 Sep 2026) This report includes spreadsheets with wholesale electricity and natural gas data from seven major trading hubs that cover most regions of the United States. The data are through September 1, 2026, and republished, with permission, from the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE).

title.original: EIA forecasts strongest four-year growth in U.S. electricity demand since 2000, fueled by data centers

items.summary: The U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) published its first energy-sector forecasts through 2027 in the January Short-Term Energy Outlook (STEO).

title.original: NASS Delays Weekly Slaughter Release

items.summary: Due to the National Day of Mourning for President James Earl Carter, Jr., USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) has rescheduled the Weekly Slaughter data release from Jan. 9 to Jan. 10 at 3 p.m. ET. Other reports scheduled for release on Jan. 10 such as Crop Production and Grain Stocks reports will be published as scheduled.

title.original: Petroleum Marketing Monthly

items.summary: (Tue, 01 Sep 2026) The September 2026 Petroleum Marketing Monthly, with data through June 2026, presents monthly and annual price and volume statistics for crude oil sales in the United States.

title.original: Natural Gas Monthly

items.summary: (Mon, 31 Aug 2026) The Natural Gas Monthly presents volume and price data each month for natural gas production, distribution, consumption, and interstate pipeline activities. NGM also reports producer-related activities and underground storage data. NGM data on 50 U.S. states and the District of Columbia are collected on EIA surveys.

title.original: EIA releases latest Short-Term Energy Outlook amid Middle East conflict

items.summary: Crude oil price movements. The Brent crude oil spot price has risen sharply following the onset of military action in the Middle East. Brent settled at $94 per barrel (b) on March 9, up about 50% from the beginning of the year and the highest since September 2023. Crude oil prices have risen as petroleum shipments through the Strait of Hormuz have fallen, and some Middle East oil production has been shut in.

title.original: Petroleum Supply Monthly

items.summary: (Tue, 01 Sep 2026) The report includes supply and disposition of crude oil and petroleum products on the national and regional levels. The data series describe production, imports and exports, movements, and inventories.

title.original: Petroleum Supply Annual

items.summary: (Tue, 01 Sep 2026) The report includes includes final annual data for the supply and disposition of crude oil and petroleum products.

title.original: USDA-NASS Crop Progress report delayed until Nov. 29

items.summary: Due to system outages, USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service delayed the release of today’s scheduled Crop Progress report until tomorrow, Nov. 29, at 4 p.m. EST.

title.original: USDA Crop Progress report delayed until 5pm ET

items.summary: USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) is delaying today’s Crop Progress report one hour until, April 5 at 5 p.m. ET.

title.original: USDA NASS Discontinues County Level Estimates for Selected Crops

items.summary: The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) will no longer publish county level estimates for dry edible beans, flaxseed, hay (alfalfa and other), potatoes, sugarbeets, sugarcane, sunflower (non-oil and oil varieties) and tobacco. In addition, NASS will discontinue county estimates based on irrigated/non-irrigated practices for all crops. These changes are effective beginning with the 2019 crop year.

title.original: EIA raises natural gas price forecast following increased heating demand amid severe winter weather

items.summary: Natural gas prices rose sharply in January, averaging $7.72 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), as cold weather increased heating demand, reduced production, and led to record storage withdrawals during Winter Storm Fern. The drawdown for the week ending January 30 was the largest weekly net withdrawal recorded in the history of EIA's Weekly Natural Gas Storage Report.

title.original: EIA releases the Annual Energy Outlook 2026

items.summary: The Annual Energy Outlook 2026 (AEO2026) explores medium- and long-term alternative futures in the United States through 2050. AEO2026 enables the public to explore a suite of alternative pathways for our energy future depending on assumptions made about markets, technological breakthroughs, and policy. It includes a narrative report, as well as the full set of data tables and visualizations, assumptions and methodologies, and detailed descriptions of the 11 cases we ran to explore these alternative futures.

title.original: NASS discontinues select 2024 data collection programs and reports

items.summary: The USDA’s National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) is canceling the July Cattle report and discontinuing the Cotton Objective Yield Survey, as well as all County Estimates for Crops and Livestock beginning with the 2024 production year. The decision to discontinue these surveys and reports was not made lightly, but was necessary, given appropriated budget levels.

title.original: EIA launches pilot survey on energy use at data centers

items.summary: EIA is launching three voluntary pilot field studies to evaluate energy consumption in data centers, with web-based pilot surveys in Texas and Washington state as well as in-person interviews in Northern Virginia and Washington, DC.
